headline: Approved HVAC screening and fencing style for 8 Canal Street; Courtland LLC case at 72 Concord Street not heard due to applicant absence.
summary: The commission approved minutes from July 27, 2026 with a correction. The Courtland, LLC case at 72 Concord Street was tabled again because the applicant did not attend; it will be heard September 28, 2026. For 8 Canal Street, the commission approved screening for rooftop HVAC units to match existing porch balustrades in a widow's walk formation, and approved a fencing style under option 2 in a rod iron style.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 27, 2026 meeting with a correction to the heading date.
Approved screening of rooftop HVAC utilities at 8 Canal Street to match existing porch balustrades in a widow's walk formation, 5-0-0.
Approved the fencing style under option 2, the 'Rod Iron Style,' for 8 Canal Street, 5-0-0.

decision_evidence.quote: MOTION by Mr. Barrett to approve the minutes with the correction of the heading that reads June 27, 2026, to July 27, 2026... MOTION CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY BY VERBAL ROLL CALL OF THE MEMBERS.

Ald. Klee made a motion to approve the screening of the utilities matching the design of the existing balustrades located below on the building porch areas in a widow's walk formation... The motion passed 5-0-0.
Ald. Klee made a motion to approve the fencing style listed under option 2 in the "Rod Iron Style," but not necessarily the need to use actual rod iron materials... The motion passed 5-0-0.

HDC Meeting August 24, 2026                              Page 1 of 5 
 
NASHUA HISTORIC DISTRICT COMMISSION 
 
Monday, August 24, 2026, 6:00 p.m., City Hall, Room 208  
 
HDC Members: 
  
 Robert Vorbach 
 Chris Barrett 
 Paige Hultman 
 Alderwoman Patricia Klee 
 Larry Hirsch 
  
 Also present:  
 
 Scott McPhie, Planner 1 
   
MINUTES: 
 
July 27, 2026: 
 
MOTION by Mr. Barrett to approve the minutes with the correction of the heading that reads June 
27, 2026, to July 27, 2026. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Vorbach 
 
MOTION CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY BY VERBAL ROLL CALL OF THE MEMBERS.   
 
 
OLD BUSINESS:  
1.   The Courtland, LLC(Owner) 72 Concord Street (Sheet 65 Lot 91) requesting the 
following: replacing all windows with new vinyl windows with simulated divided 
lite, remove and replace siding and replace with wooden clapboard siding, repair 
and restore third floor porch, replace all diamond pattern lattice with square 
pattern lattice, repair/replace porch roof and porch ceiling, and install a new 
porch roof finished with architectural asphalt shingles or standing seem metal 
roof. RB zone, Ward 3. Tabled from the July 27, 2026 meeting to obtain paint 
samples.) 
 
The applicant neglected to attend the meeting; therefore, the case was not heard. The 
Chair indicated they would be attending the next meeting on September 28, 2026. 
 
 
NEW BUSINESS: 
 
1. The Tousley Fam Rev Trust, Todd & Bette Jean Tousley (Owners), Todd Tousley 
(Applicant), 8 Canal Street (Sheet 43 Lot 39), requesting approval for existing 
mini-split HVAC condenser units serving 7 residential units on the roof, and one
HDC Meeting August 24, 2026                              Page 2 of 5 
condenser at the rear of unit 104; also for metal fencing along the sidewalk. D-
1/MU Zone, Ward 3. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
  Robert Vorbach 
  Chris Barrett 
  Paige Hultman 
  Alderwoman Patricia Klee 
  Larry Hirsch 
   
 
 
Mr. Tousley indicated he was in the process of applying for his building permit, and the building 
department discovered that additions were made to his plan, resulting in the need for further 
review. The specific changes were adding unscreened HVAC units on the roof and the need for a 
safety fence along some of the property, both of which require Historical District Commission 
review due to changes in the exterior appearance of the property. 
 
Alderman Patricia Klee asked if he needed to go to the Planning Board. He replied no. 
 
A discussion ensued on the aesthetic considerations of using mini-splits HVAC equipment versus 
placing the equipment on a roof. 
 
Mr. Vorbach cited a recent example of a home on Concord Street that recently added such mini-
split devices, which detracted from the exterior character of the building and therefore was not in 
character with the historic district. He said the rooftop location was preferred. 
 
Mr. Barrett asked if the equipment could be screened. Mr. McPhie added it's generally required to 
screen all utilities. 
 
Mr. Vorbach explained that there are purposefully made screening materials that would not require 
you to build the screening from the ground up. 
 
Mr. Tousley then proceeded to express concerns due to financial constraints.  
 
Mr. Hirsch then asked the Commission if they wanted to see samples of the screening, as that could 
delay the project and add additional costs at the applicant's expense.  Can we be more specific 
tonight and approve a solution to reduce delays for the applicant?  
 
A discussion ensued concerning delays to the ongoing project. 
 
Mr. Vorbach praised the applicant for his efforts thus far, but indicated it would be up to the 
discretion of the Commission if they wanted to leave the materials and aesthetics up to the 
discretion of the applicant and staff. 
 
Alderman Klee and Mr. Hirsh indicated at the Planning Board level such a decision is left to staff 
discretion.
HDC Meeting August 24, 2026                              Page 3 of 5 
Mr. McPhie added that it may be acceptable to the Planning Board, but one of the major functions 
of the Historic District Commission is to decide on materials and aesthetics, and that he would feel 
uncomfortable making that decision for them.  
 
Mr. Tousley then asked whether the Commission could be more specific in describing the 
screening materials you are requesting. 
 
Mr. Vorbach then reviewed the pictures provided concerning the visibility from the street. The 
pictures you provided do not show the utilities being very visible from the street.  
 
Mr. McPhie then added that Dawn Michaud from the Building Department witnessed the roof 
Units from the Library across the river, and I drove down each of the streets, and the roof utilities 
were clearly visible from the streets in that additional area. 
 
An additional discussion ensued, and a positive option came out of the discussion to request the 
roof equipment be screened with the same materials as used for the porch balustrades already on 
the house in a widow's walk formation. Mr. Hirsh then asked the applicant if that was acceptable 
to him.  Mr. Tousley said no, but understands the commission can request the screening. 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
 
No One 
 
Speaking Against: 
 
No One 
 
A discussion of the second part of the application concerning the fencing material occurred. 
 
Mr. Tousley indicated he was not aware he needed fencing until the City told him to add it to meet 
code.  He quickly added the fencing to prevent any City enforcement actions. Mr. Tousley said he 
was unaware he needed to come back to the HDC for fencing until told by the building department.  
 
Mr. Tousley then requested what material the Commission would be looking for. 
 
Mr. Vorbach said the Commission is not as concerned about the materials used other than vinyl, 
which would look terrible, but was more concerned about the aesthetics.  For instance, chain link 
would not go with the aesthetic, as that is more industrial-looking.  The other option you provided 
showing the look of cast iron would be fine.  
 
Mr. Tousley agreed the second option provided would be his preferred choice as well. 
 
A discussion ensued concerning the lack of durability and the ugliness of vinyl fencing and 
screening in general. All present agreed that vinyl was not an appropriate material.  
 
Speaking in Favor: 
 
No One 
 
Speaking Against:
HDC Meeting August 24, 2026                              Page 4 of 5 
No One 
 
END OF THE PUBLIC HEARING: BEGINNING OF THE PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Ald. Klee made a motion to approve the screening of the utilities matching the design of the 
existing balustrades located below on the building porch areas in a widow's walk formation.  The 
motion was seconded by Mr. Hirsch. 
 
The motion passed 5-0-0. 
  
 
Ald. Klee made a motion to approve the fencing style listed under option 2 in the “Rod Iron Style,” 
but not necessarily the need to use actual rod iron materials.  The motion was seconded by Mr. 
Vorbach. 
 
The motion passed 5-0-0. 
 
To clarify the decision made tonight, Mr. McPhie indicated clearly that under the Land Use Code 
Section 190-22 (A) (2), the HDC has the authority to request such changes as they did tonight and 
then read the full criteria into the record.  
  
a. The historical or architectural value of the building or structure and its settings; and 
 
b. The general compatibility of exterior design, arrangement, texture and materials proposed 
to be used in relationship to the existing building or structure and its settings or if new 
construction, to the surrounding area, and 
 
c. The general size and scale of new construction in relationship to the existing surroundings, 
including such factors as the building's overall height, width, street frontage, number of 
stories, types of roofs, façade openings (windows & doors), architectural details; and 
 
d. Other factors, including yards, off-street parking spaces, location of entrance drives, 
sidewalks, extent and coverage of pavement, signs and landscaping, which might affect the 
character of any    building or structure within the district, and any other factor which relates 
to the appropriate settings for such structure or grouping of structures; and 
 
e. The special character of the area including whether or not it is primarily residential or 
commercial; and 
 
f. The economic activity of the building and the needs of that activity, and as it relates to the 
welfare of the community.  
 
 Mr. Tousley then made one request that there be better communication between the HDC and the 
Building Department, as it would have been better if all these items were addressed at the initial 
meeting.  
 
Mr. McPhie added that it is always best to show everything on the original drawings.  
The Commission agreed that communications can always improve.   
 
Mr. McPhie added that he had spoken to the building department just before the meeting and asked 
if the project had any other issues if approved at tonight's HDC meeting, also indicating he does
HDC Meeting August 24, 2026                              Page 5 of 5 
have a good working relationship with the building department and will work toward improving 
that communication with the HDC as well. 
 
Mr. Hirsh suggested creating a checklist similar to the PB mylar sheets for the HDC would be 
helpful.  Ald. Klee concurred with the checklist suggestion  
 
Mr. McPhie said the Planning Department already uses an extensive checklist, and he could look 
into creating something that was HDC-specific.  
 
Mr. Vorbach thanked the applicant and said to feel free to call him concerning the application of 
the screening materials. 
   
ADJOURN  
 
MOTION by Mr. Vorbach   6:52 PM 
 
MOTION CARRIED
